message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: documentation

on: [push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch]

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  docs:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      - name: Cache pip dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/pip
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          pip install sphinx sphinx_rtd_theme sphinx-design myst_parser
      - name: Check the Python and C++ versions of the examples
        run: |
          python3 scripts/generate_doc_snippets.py
          git diff --exit-code -- doc/examples
      - name: Sphinx build
        run: |
          sphinx-build doc _build
      - name: Deploy to GitHub Pages
        uses: peaceiris/actions-gh-pages@v3
        if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/master' }}
        with:
          publish_branch: gh-pages
          github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          publish_dir: _build/
          force_orphan: true",
  "rationale": "The workflow installs Python documentation dependencies (sphinx, sphinx_rtd_theme, sphinx-design, myst_parser) via pip on every run with no dependency cache. The repository has a pyproject.toml, so a pip cache keyed on its hash is applicable. Evidence from experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2 (measured CI workflow on fork) shows adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip with key ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }} and restore-keys. The change is inserted after setup-python and before Install dependencies, preserving all existing steps, coverage, permissions, and the deploy job; it adds no privileged actions, secrets, publishing changes, or new network access.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
